MPs Speaking:Mr Chew Swee Kee (Minister for Education); Mr M. P. D. Nair (Assistant Minister to the Chief Secretary); Mr Oon Khye Kiang (Acting Financial Secretary); Mr Lee Choon Eng; Mr Lee Kuan Yew; Mr Lim Choon Mong; Sir George Oehlers (Mr Speaker);


Column: 859

SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISION
(Sessional Paper No. Cmd. 31 of 1958)


    The Acting Financial Secretary (Mr Oon Khye Kiang): Mr Speaker, Sir, I have the Governor's recommendation to proceed with the motion. I beg to move,

    That this Assembly resolves that the sum of $1,461,162 shall be supplied to the Government under the heads of expenditure and for the service specified in the Schedule contained in Sessional Paper No. Cmd. 31 of 1958. Sir, the Schedule consists of a list of ten applications for supplementary provision amount to $1,461,162. The reasons for these supplementary votes are given in detail in the Sessional Paper. There are two items which involve a substantial sum of money. One of them refers to the construction of four secondary schools for which $1,000,000 has been provided for this year. Work has progressed faster than was envisaged at the time when the Estimates were prepared. It is anticipated that a total sum of $2.1 million will be required for progress payments during the year, and supplementary provision of about $1.1 million will be required. These schools are urgently needed and when they are completed will meet the present demand in the various districts. The second one refers to the Muslim Welfare Home for destitute Muslim women. This project has been under consideration for some time. A token provision was provided in the Estimates to enable planning to be carried out. This has been completed and it has been decided to give this project top priority. The Home will be built at Jalan Eunos and, when completed, will meet a long-felt want.

    Sir, I beg to move.

    Mr Chew Swee Kee: Sir, I second it.

    Motion committed to Committee of Supply.

    Motion and Schedule considered in Committee of Supply.

[Mr Speaker in the Chair]



4.00 p.m.
